scene: a narrow stone chamber at night, brick wall behind
light: a single clay fire bowl on the left side only, warm uplight raking across the stele face, deep shadow on the right
prompt: A single black basalt stele stands upright in a narrow stone chamber at night. On top of the stele sits a carved Assyrian winged sun disc, symmetrical with downturned wings, chiselled in low relief. The face of the stele below the disc is smooth blank dark stone, catching raking warm light. On the LEFT side only, one low clay fire bowl burns, its flame throwing warm amber uplight across the stele surface and the brick wall behind; the right side of the frame falls into deep black. Ash and fine dust sit on the stone base, edges worn smooth by time. The chamber is empty and still. Low-key lighting from a single motivated source, crushed blacks, fine 35mm grain.

scene: a dim museum gallery at night, one illuminated display case
light: cool ceiling spot above the case, a single warm glow rising from inside the case
prompt: A dim museum gallery at night. One young woman in a cream knit sweater stands alone in front of an illuminated glass display case, seen from behind and slightly to the side so her profile edge is visible. Her right hand rests flat against the glass. Inside the case a black carved stone stele lies on a plinth, and the glass carries a reflection of that carved stone face right beside her hand. She is the only person in the frame; the glass reflects carved stone and the dark gallery. Cool ceiling light above, one warm glow rising from inside the case, polished floor catching a faint sheen. The gallery is empty and quiet. Fine 35mm grain, black point slightly lifted.
